"""
Browser session tools for codx-junior agents.

These tools let the LLM drive the same real Chromium browser the user is
watching and controlling through the live VNC view (managed by
``BrowserManager``).  There is no separate "AI browser": user and AI share one
page, one set of cookies and one history.

The browser container also mounts the project folders under
``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` and writes its downloads inside the project,
so the agent and the user exchange files with the project instead of being
isolated in the container.

Tools
-----
- ``start_session``      – create & start (or resume) a browser session.
- ``browse_action``      – navigate / click / fill / execute JS / read text /
                           back / forward / refresh / wait / press / select /
                           hover / scroll / links / tabs (list, open, switch,
                           close).
- ``get_screenshot``     – capture a PNG screenshot of the current page.
- ``get_source_code``    – return the current page HTML.
- ``browser_activity``   – recent user/AI actions on the session (co-browsing
                           awareness).
- ``finish_session``     – stop (default) or delete the session. Stopping keeps
                           the Chromium profile; deleting removes it too.

Settings
--------
Every tool receives ``settings`` (CODXJuniorSettings) through the
``project_settings`` injection mechanism and ``chat_id`` (from the running
SmolAgent) when its signature declares it.  All tools are ``async`` and return
:class:`ToolResponse` so the chat can render a user-facing summary while the
model receives machine-readable content.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings
from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs
from .model import ToolResponse

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Settings metadata applied to every browser tool in the ``TOOLS`` registry.
#: Both ``async`` and ``is_async`` keys are provided for compatibility with the
#: two conventions present in the codebase.
BROWSER_TOOL_SETTINGS: Dict[str, Any] = {
    "async": True,
    "is_async": True,
    "project_settings": True,
    "dual_response": True,
    "scope": "chat",
    # Browser state changes between calls: never serve a cached result.
    "cache": False,
}

#: Hard cap on the HTML returned by ``get_source_code`` (keeps LLM context sane).
MAX_SOURCE_CHARS = 60000
#: Hard cap on visible text returned by ``browse_action(text)``.
MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 12000

#: Actions that operate on tabs instead of the current page content.
TAB_ACTIONS = ("tabs", "new_tab", "switch_tab", "close_tab")

#: Actions that can use an explicit tab index.
INDEX_ACTIONS = ("switch_tab", "close_tab")


def _settings_from(kwargs: Dict[str, Any]) -> CODXJuniorSettings:
    """Extract and validate injected project settings."""
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")
    return settings


def _manager(settings: CODXJuniorSettings):
    """Build a BrowserManager for the given settings."""
    from codx.junior.browser.browser_manager import BrowserManager
    return BrowserManager(settings)


def _resolve_session(manager, session_id: Optional[str] = None, chat_id: Optional[str] = None):
    """Resolve a session by id, falling back to the chat's shared session."""
    session = manager.get_session(session_id) if session_id else None
    if not session and chat_id:
        session = manager.get_session_for_chat(chat_id)
    return session


def _shared_folder_lines(session) -> List[str]:
    """Describe every folder mounted in the session (empty when none)."""
    return [
        f"  - {share.name or share.folder or '/'} → {share.mount_path}"
        f"{' (read-only)' if share.readonly else ''}"
        f"  [project: {share.folder or '/'}]"
        for share in session.shared_folders
    ]


def _summary(session) -> str:
    """Build a short human-readable summary of a session."""
    folders = ", ".join(share.mount_path for share in session.shared_folders) or "(none)"
    return (
        f"session_id={session.id}\n"
        f"name={session.name or '(unnamed)'}\n"
        f"status={session.status}\n"
        f"chats={', '.join(session.chat_ids) or '(none)'}\n"
        f"live_view={session.vnc_url or '(starting)'}\n"
        f"home={session.home_path or '(not shared)'}\n"
        f"mounted_folders={folders}\n"
        f"downloads={session.downloads_mount or '(none)'} (host: {session.downloads_path or '-'})\n"
        f"current_url={session.current_url or '(blank)'}\n"
        f"current_title={session.current_title or '(blank)'}"
    )


def _sharing_note(session) -> str:
    """Describe the folder mapping for the LLM (empty when nothing is shared)."""
    if not session.shares_files():
        return ""
    lines = _shared_folder_lines(session)
    note = ""
    if lines:
        note = (
            "The browser has these project folders mounted (open them with "
            "file://<mount_path>/<file>):\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
        )
    if session.downloads_path:
        note += (
            f"Downloads are saved inside the project at '{session.downloads_path}' "
            f"(browser path '{session.downloads_mount}')."
        )
    return note.strip()


def _persist_to_chat(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, session, chat_id: Optional[str]) -> None:
    """Persist a session into its chat's meta_data (best effort)."""
    if not chat_id:
        return
    try:
        from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager
        chat_manager = ChatManager(settings)
        chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat_id)
        if chat:
            _manager(settings).save_session_to_chat(session, chat)
            chat_manager.save_chat(chat)
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning("Could not persist browser session to chat %s: %s", chat_id, ex)


async def start_session(
    name: str = None,
    chat_id: str = None,
    initial_url: str = None,
    description: str = None,
    share_project: bool = None,
    share_folders: List[str] = None,
    downloads_folder: str = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Start (or resume) a browser session connected to the current chat.

    Creates and starts an isolated Chromium container.  The returned
    ``session_id`` is used by the other browser tools, and ``live_view`` is the
    URL the user opens to watch and control the same browser.

    Project folders are mounted inside the container under
    ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` and every download is saved inside the
    project, so files are shared between the user, the AI and the project.

    Args:
        name: Human-readable session name (defaults to a timestamped name).
        chat_id: Associated chat id (injected by SmolAgent); used to reuse the
            chat's existing session and to make it visible in the chat UI.
        initial_url: Optional URL opened when the browser starts.
        description: Optional free-form description of the session.
        share_project: Mount the whole project at ``/home/<project_name>``.
            Omit it to mount the project root only when ``share_folders`` is
            empty.
        share_folders: Project folders to mount (``["docs", "data"]``); each one
            keeps its relative path inside ``/home/<project_name>``.
        downloads_folder: Project-relative folder receiving the downloads
            (default ``.codx/browser_downloads/<session_id>``).
        **kwargs: Injected ``settings``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the session details and live-view URL.
    """
    settings = _settings_from(kwargs)
    manager = _manager(settings)

    session_name = (name or "").strip() or f"Browser {datetime.utcnow().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"

    try:
        existing = manager.get_session_for_chat(chat_id) if chat_id else None
        if existing:
            if existing.status != "running":
                try:
                    existing = await asyncio.to_thread(manager.restart_session, existing.id)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.warning("Could not restart browser session %s: %s", existing.id, ex)

            if existing and existing.status == "running":
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response=(
                        f"♻️ Browser session already running.\n"
                        f"[Open the live browser]({existing.vnc_url})\n"
                        f"```\n{_summary(existing)}\n```"
                    ),
                    llm_response=(
                        "A browser session is already running for this chat. "
                        f"Use this session_id in subsequent calls: {existing.id}. "
                        f"Live view: {existing.vnc_url}. "
                        f"{_sharing_note(existing)}"
                    ),
                )

        session = await asyncio.to_thread(
            manager.create_session,
            session_name,
            chat_id,
            initial_url,
            description,
            share_project,
            share_folders,
            None,
            downloads_folder,
        )
        _persist_to_chat(settings, session, chat_id)

        llm = (
            f"Browser session '{session.name}' started. session_id: {session.id}. "
            f"Live view (same browser the user sees): {session.vnc_url}. "
            "Use browse_action/get_screenshot/get_source_code/browser_activity "
            "with this session_id. Call finish_session when done. "
            f"{_sharing_note(session)}"
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"✅ Browser session '{session.name}' ready.\n"
                f"[Open the live browser]({session.vnc_url})\n"
                f"```\n{_summary(session)}\n```"
            ),
            llm_response=llm,
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("start_session failed: %s", ex)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Failed to start browser session: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to start browser session: {ex}",
        )


async def browse_action(
    action: str,
    url: str = None,
    selector: str = None,
    value: str = None,
    script: str = None,
    key: str = None,
    timeout: int = 5000,
    index: int = None,
    x: int = 0,
    y: int = 0,
    session_id: str = None,
    chat_id: str = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Perform an action on the shared browser page or on its tabs.

    Args:
        action: One of ``navigate``, ``click``, ``fill``, ``execute``,
            ``text``, ``links``, ``back``, ``forward``, ``refresh``, ``wait``,
            ``press``, ``select``, ``hover``, ``scroll``, ``tabs``,
            ``new_tab``, ``switch_tab``, ``close_tab``.
        url: Target URL (for ``navigate`` and ``new_tab``).
        selector: CSS selector (for element actions).
        value: Text to fill or option to select.
        script: JavaScript to run (for ``execute``; use ``return ...``).
        key: Keyboard key for ``press``.
        timeout: Timeout in milliseconds for ``wait``.
        index: Tab index (0-based) for ``switch_tab`` / ``close_tab``; omit it to
            act on the active tab.
        x: Horizontal scroll offset.
        y: Vertical scroll offset.
        session_id: Session to act on (returned by ``start_session``).
        chat_id: Alternative to ``session_id`` — resolves the chat's session.
        **kwargs: Injected ``settings``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the action result, current URL and title.
    """
    settings = _settings_from(kwargs)
    manager = _manager(settings)
    session = _resolve_session(manager, session_id=session_id, chat_id=chat_id)

    if not session:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="❌ No browser session found. Call `start_session` first.",
            llm_response="No browser session available. Start one with start_session.",
        )
    if session.status != "running":
        # A stopped container can usually be resumed without losing the profile.
        try:
            session = await asyncio.to_thread(manager.restart_session, session.id)
        except Exception as ex:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"❌ Session is not running and could not be restarted: {ex}",
                llm_response=f"Session {session.id} is not running (status: {session.status}) and restart failed: {ex}",
            )

    action = (action or "").lower().strip()
    params = {
        key_name: value
        for key_name, value in {
            "url": url,
            "selector": selector,
            "value": value,
            "script": script,
            "key": key,
            "timeout": timeout,
            "index": index,
            "x": x,
            "y": y,
        }.items()
        if value is not None
    }
    started_at = time.monotonic()
    browser = None
    try:
        browser = await manager.connect_browser(session)
        if action == "navigate":
            if not url:
                raise ValueError("url is required for navigate")
            title = await browser.navigate(url)
            data = f"navigated to {url}\ntitle: {title}"

        elif action == "click":
            if not selector:
                raise ValueError("selector is required for click")
            await browser.click(selector)
            data = f"clicked {selector}"

        elif action == "fill":
            if not selector or value is None:
                raise ValueError("selector and value are required for fill")
            await browser.fill(selector, value)
            data = f"filled {selector}"

        elif action == "execute":
            if not script:
                raise ValueError("script is required for execute")
            result = await browser.execute_script(script)
            data = f"script result: {result}"

        elif action in ("text", "read"):
            text = (await browser.get_text() or "").strip()
            data = f"page text:\n{text[:MAX_TEXT_CHARS]}"

        elif action == "links":
            links = await browser.get_links()
            lines = [f"- {link.get('text') or '(no text)'} → {link.get('href')}" for link in links[:200]]
            data = f"links ({len(links)}):\n" + "\n".join(lines)

        elif action == "back":
            title = await browser.go_back()
            data = f"went back\ntitle: {title}"

        elif action == "forward":
            title = await browser.go_forward()
            data = f"went forward\ntitle: {title}"

        elif action == "refresh":
            title = await browser.reload()
            data = f"page refreshed\ntitle: {title}"

        elif action == "wait":
            if not selector:
                raise ValueError("selector is required for wait")
            await browser.wait_for_selector(selector, timeout=timeout or 5000)
            data = f"element appeared: {selector}"

        elif action == "press":
            if not selector or not key:
                raise ValueError("selector and key are required for press")
            await browser.press(selector, key)
            data = f"pressed {key} on {selector}"

        elif action == "select":
            if not selector or value is None:
                raise ValueError("selector and value are required for select")
            await browser.select(selector, value)
            data = f"selected {value} on {selector}"

        elif action == "hover":
            if not selector:
                raise ValueError("selector is required for hover")
            await browser.hover(selector)
            data = f"hovered {selector}"

        elif action == "scroll":
            await browser.scroll(x=x or 0, y=y or 0)
            data = f"scrolled by x={x or 0}, y={y or 0}"

        elif action == "tabs":
            tabs = await browser_tabs.list_tabs(browser)
            data = f"open tabs ({len(tabs)}):\n" + browser_tabs.format_tabs(tabs)

        elif action == "new_tab":
            tab = await browser_tabs.open_tab(browser, url)
            data = (
                f"opened tab [{tab['index']}] {tab['title'] or '(untitled)'}\n"
                f"url: {tab['url']}"
            )

        elif action == "switch_tab":
            tab = await browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, index)
            data = (
                f"switched to tab [{tab['index']}] {tab['title'] or '(untitled)'}\n"
                f"url: {tab['url']}"
            )

        elif action == "close_tab":
            tab = await browser_tabs.close_tab(browser, index)
            data = (
                f"closed tab [{tab['closed_index']}] "
                f"{tab['closed_title'] or tab['closed_url']}\n"
                f"active tab is now [{tab['index']}] {tab['title'] or '(untitled)'}\n"
                f"url: {tab['url']}"
            )

        else:
            raise ValueError(
                "unknown action '%s' (use navigate|click|fill|execute|text|links|"
                "back|forward|refresh|wait|press|select|hover|scroll|"
                "tabs|new_tab|switch_tab|close_tab)" % action
            )

        session.mark_active()
        manager.save_session(session)
        manager.log_activity(
            session,
            actor="ai",
            action=action,
            chat_id=chat_id,
            params=params,
            url=session.current_url,
            title=session.current_title,
            duration_ms=(time.monotonic() - started_at) * 1000,
            result={"message": data[:1000]},
        )
        logger.info("browse_action '%s' completed for session %s", action, session.id[:8])

        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"✅ `{action}` done on session {session.id[:8]}.\n\n{data}\n\n"
                f"URL: {session.current_url or '(blank)'}\nTitle: {session.current_title or '(blank)'}"
            ),
            llm_response=(
                f"Action '{action}' on session {session.id} succeeded.\n{data}\n"
                f"URL: {session.current_url or '(blank)'}\nTitle: {session.current_title or '(blank)'}"
            ),
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("browse_action failed: %s", ex)
        manager.log_activity(
            session,
            actor="ai",
            action=action or "unknown",
            chat_id=chat_id,
            params=params,
            success=False,
            error=str(ex),
            duration_ms=(time.monotonic() - started_at) * 1000,
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ `{action}` failed: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"Action '{action}' on session {session.id} failed: {ex}",
        )
    finally:
        if browser is not None:
            await browser.close()

            llm_response=f"No activity recorded for session {session.id}.",
        )

    lines = []
    for entry in entries:
        actor = entry.get("actor") or "?"
        action = entry.get("action") or "?"
        status = "ok" if entry.get("success", True) else "error"
        url = entry.get("url") or ""
        lines.append(f"- [{entry.get('ts')}] {actor}: {action} ({status}) {url}".rstrip())
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=f"🧾 Recent activity for session {session.id[:8]}:\n{text}",
        llm_response=f"Recent activity for session {session.id}:\n{text}",
    )


async def finish_session(
    session_id: str = None,
    chat_id: str = None,
    delete: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Finish a browser session. Stopping keeps its profile; deleting removes it.

    Args:
        session_id: Session to finish (or ``chat_id`` to resolve it).
        chat_id: Alternative to ``session_id``.
        delete: When True the container is removed and the session folder
            (including its Chromium profile) is deleted. When False (default)
            the container is only stopped and the profile is preserved for a
            later restart.
        **kwargs: Injected ``settings``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the finish result.
    """
    settings = _settings_from(kwargs)
    manager = _manager(settings)
    session = _resolve_session(manager, session_id=session_id, chat_id=chat_id)

    if not session:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="❌ No browser session found to finish.",
            llm_response="No browser session found to finish.",
        )

    try:
        if delete:
            await asyncio.to_thread(manager.delete_session, session.id)
            verb = "deleted"
        else:
            await asyncio.to_thread(manager.stop_session, session.id)
            verb = "stopped"

        logger.info("finish_session: %s session %s", verb, session.id[:8])
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"🧹 Browser session {session.id[:8]} {verb}.",
            llm_response=(
                f"Browser session {session.id} {verb}. "
                + ("Profile preserved." if not delete else "Profile deleted with the session.")
                + (
                    f" Downloaded files stay in the project at '{session.downloads_path}'."
                    if session.downloads_path else ""
                )
            ),
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("finish_session failed: %s", ex)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Failed to finish session: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"Failed to finish session {session.id}: {ex}",
        )

"""Tests for the browser tab primitives used by the ``browse_action`` tool.

Playwright is not required: the tests drive fake pages/contexts that mimic the
parts of the API the tab layer relies on (``context.pages``, ``new_page()``,
``page.title()``, ``page.bring_to_front()``, ``page.close()``).
"""

import asyncio

import pytest

from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs


class _FakeSession:
    """Minimal BrowserSession stand-in (only the fields the tab layer touches)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.current_url = None
        self.current_title = None
        self.active_calls = 0

    def mark_active(self):
        self.active_calls += 1


class _FakePage:
    def __init__(self, url="about:blank", title="", context=None):
        self.url = url
        self._title = title
        self._closed = False
        self.context = context
        self.front_calls = 0

    async def title(self):
        return self._title

    def is_closed(self):
        return self._closed

    async def bring_to_front(self):
        self.front_calls += 1

    async def close(self):
        self._closed = True
        if self.context and self in self.context.pages:
            self.context.pages.remove(self)


class _FakeContext:
    def __init__(self, pages):
        self.pages = list(pages)

    async def new_page(self):
        page = _FakePage(context=self)
        self.pages.append(page)
        return page


class _FakeBrowser:
    def __init__(self, pages=None):
        pages = list(pages) if pages else [_FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")]
        self.context = _FakeContext(pages)
        for page in pages:
            page.context = self.context
        self.page = pages[0]
        self.session = _FakeSession()
        self.navigations = []

    async def navigate(self, url):
        self.navigations.append(url)
        self.page.url = url
        self.page._title = f"title of {url}"
        return self.page._title


def _run(coroutine):
    return asyncio.run(coroutine)


def test_lists_tabs_and_marks_the_active_one():
    first = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    second = _FakePage(url="https://b.test", title="B")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([first, second])
    browser.page = second

    tabs = _run(browser_tabs.list_tabs(browser))

    assert [tab["index"] for tab in tabs] == [0, 1]
    assert [tab["url"] for tab in tabs] == ["https://a.test", "https://b.test"]
    assert [tab["title"] for tab in tabs] == ["A", "B"]
    assert [tab["active"] for tab in tabs] == [False, True]


def test_open_tab_creates_navigates_and_focuses_a_page():
    browser = _FakeBrowser()

    tab = _run(browser_tabs.open_tab(browser, "https://new.test"))

    assert tab["index"] == 1
    assert tab["url"] == "https://new.test"
    assert tab["active"] is True
    assert browser.navigations == ["https://new.test"]
    assert browser.page is browser.context.pages[1]
    assert browser.page.front_calls == 1
    assert browser.session.current_url == "https://new.test"
    assert browser.session.current_title == "title of https://new.test"


def test_open_tab_without_url_keeps_a_blank_tab():
    browser = _FakeBrowser()

    tab = _run(browser_tabs.open_tab(browser))

    assert tab["url"] == "about:blank"
    assert browser.navigations == []
    assert browser.context.pages[-1] is browser.page


def test_switch_tab_changes_the_active_page():
    first = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    second = _FakePage(url="https://b.test", title="B")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([first, second])

    tab = _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 1))

    assert tab["index"] == 1
    assert tab["active"] is True
    assert browser.page is second
    assert second.front_calls == 1
    assert browser.session.current_url == "https://b.test"
    assert browser.session.current_title == "B"

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, 5))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _run(browser_tabs.switch_tab(browser, "first"))

    first = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    second = _FakePage(url="https://b.test", title="B")
    third = _FakePage(url="https://c.test", title="C")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([first, second, third])

    tab = _run(browser_tabs.close_tab(browser, 1))

    assert tab["closed_index"] == 1
    assert tab["closed_url"] == "https://b.test"
    assert second._closed is True
    assert browser.context.pages == [first, third]
    # The tab that took the freed position becomes active
    assert tab["index"] == 1
    assert browser.page is third
    assert browser.session.current_url == "https://c.test"


def test_close_tab_defaults_to_the_active_tab():
    first = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")

    browser = _FakeBrowser([first, second])

    class _Disconnected:

    browser = _FakeBrowser([first, second])

    tabs = [
        {"index": 0, "url": "https://a.test", "title": "A", "active": False},
        {"index": 1, "url": "https://b.test", "title": "", "active": True},

    text = browser_tabs.format_tabs(tabs)

    assert "- [0] A — https://a.test" in text
    assert "* [1] (untitled) — https://b.test" in text

"""
BrowserSession — data model for browser session state.

Stores session configuration and connection info, persisted in Chat.meta_data["browser"]
and in session folder as <session_id>.session JSON file.

A session is shared between chats: ``chat_ids`` holds every chat currently connected
to the session while ``name`` is the human-readable label provided at creation.

The session also stores the **project folder mapping**: any number of project folders
are bind mounted inside the browser container under ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>``
and the browser's downloads are written into a project folder, so the user (live VNC
view) and the AI exchange files with the project instead of being isolated in the
container.

    ``host_path`` the absolute host folder and ``mount_path`` the path the same
    folder gets inside the container (``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` unless
    the caller asked for a custom mount point).
    """

    id: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Immutable share identifier (auto-generated)"
    )
    name: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,

    )
    folder: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Project-relative folder ('' or None means the project root)"
    )
    host_path: str = Field(
        description="Absolute host folder bind mounted into the container"
    )
    mount_path: str = Field(
        description="Path of the folder inside the container (e.g. /home/proj/docs)"
    )

        default=False,

Because `BROWSE_ACTION_TOOL_JSON` is a module-level dict imported **by reference**, editing its `enum` and adding the `index` property inside `browser_tools.py` is automatically what the registry serves. No import line, no `TOOLS` entry, no `__all__`, no profile edit, and above all **no rewrite of the 1639-line `tools/__init__.py`**.

## The one action required

**Restart the API process.** `TOOLS` is materialised at import time; a running worker keeps the old schema in memory even though the file changed. (Not a registration issue — a reload issue.)

## When registration *would* be required

Only if you split the tabs into a **new tool name** (e.g. `browser_tabs`), then all three are mandatory:

1. `browser_tools.py` → new `async def browser_tabs(...)` + a `BROWSER_TABS_TOOL_JSON` constant (Anthropic-style `{"type":"function","function":{...}}`, no `tool_call` inside).
2. `tools/__init__.py` → two hunks: the import and an entry in `TOOLS` (or `*BROWSER_TABS_TOOLS` if you prefer the `BROWSER_SCRIPT_TOOLS` spread convention — **no** lazy `ensure_registered()` helper).
3. `browser.profile` → add `"browser_tabs"` to `tools:`, otherwise the agent never receives it.

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- **Do not add `ensure_registered()`.** The project convention is explicit import + spread; lazy registration creates import cycles and ungreppable wiring.

"""
Tab (page) management for the shared browser session.

The browser container is a real Chromium window: the user watches it through the
live VNC view while the AI drives it over CDP, so tabs are a **shared** resource.
Opening, selecting and closing them must be visible in that same window.

``Browser`` (``codx.junior.browser.browser``) owns the connection and the page
automation primitives; this module adds the tab primitives it deliberately does
not cover, operating on a connected ``Browser``:

    tabs = await list_tabs(browser)         # every tab + active flag
    tab  = await open_tab(browser, url)     # new tab, navigated and focused
    tab  = await switch_tab(browser, index) # move the AI (and the user) to it
    tab  = await close_tab(browser, index)  # close one, activate the next

Conventions
-----------
- the *tab index* is the position of the page in ``context.pages`` (stable while
  no tab is opened or closed); that is what the agent tools expose;
- ``browser.page`` always points at the tab the AI drives;
- every selection is brought to front, so the live view shows the tab the AI is
  working on (co-browsing);
- the last tab is never closed: closing it would close the browser window the
  user is watching.
"""

import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Hard cap on the tabs an agent may open (they are all visible to the user).
MAX_TABS = 20


def _session_label(browser) -> str:
    """Short session id used in the log lines (never raises)."""
    session = getattr(browser, "session", None)
    return str(getattr(session, "id", "") or "?")[:8]

I'll read the current browser connection and tab code before changing anything — the fix has to plug into the existing connect path.Everything I need is read. Here is the design and the changes. ## 1. Root cause Chromium **exits when its last window closes**. The container stays alive (`/init` + the desktop session survive), so: - the live VNC view keeps rendering, but the browser window is gone; - the CDP proxy has nothing to forward to → `connect_over_cdp` fails; - `Browser.connect()` creates a page only when a *context* exists — with Chromium dead there is no context at all, so every tool call fails and the session is effectively lost. `tabs.close_tab` already refused to close the last tab, but nothing protected the window from the **user** closing tabs by hand, and nothing healed a session after it happened. ## 2. Fix (three layers) | Layer | Mechanism | |---|---| | **Prevention** | A protected **keep-alive tab** per session (`about:blank#codx-keep-alive`, titled *"codx-junior · keep this tab open"*), created right after the container starts and re-created on every connection if missing. Closing every other tab leaves the window alive. | | **Refusal** | `close_tab` refuses the keep-alive tab (besides the existing "never the last tab" rule). | | **Self-healing** | `BrowserManager.connect_browser` restarts the browser process once when the CDP connection fails (stop + start the container → the entrypoint relaunches Chromium with the mounted profile), then reconnects. `restart_session` (REST/UI restart) now always relaunches Chromium, and recreates the guard tab. | | **Recovery of the page** | `tabs.ensure_page` reopens a tab (restoring `session.current_url`) whenever `context.pages` is empty. | No docker API changed: recovery reuses `stop_container(remove=False)` + `restart_container`, which already re-runs the entrypoint and re-resolves `debug_url`. ## 3. Changes summary | File | Change | |---|---| | `codx/junior/browser/tabs.py` | keep-alive tab (`is_keep_alive_page`, `keep_alive_page`, `ensure_keep_alive_tab`), `ensure_page` recovery, `close_tab` guard, `list_tabs`/`switch_tab` recovery, `keep_alive` flag in descriptors | | `codx/junior/browser/browser_manager.py` | `connect_browser` auto-recovery + guard tab, `restart_session` relaunches Chromium, `_restart_browser`, `_open_keep_alive_tab` (eager at creation, background when inside a loop) | | `tests/browser/test_browser_keepalive.py` | **new** – guard tab, recovery, close protections, manager retry | `browser.py`, `docker_browser_manager.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `tools/__init__.py` and the profile are untouched (no new tool: `browse_action` `tabs`/`close_tab` already registered). """ Tab (page) management for the shared browser session. The browser container is a real Chromium window: the user watches it through the live VNC view while the AI drives it over CDP, so tabs are a **shared** resource. Opening, selecting and closing them must be visible in that same window. ``Browser`` (``codx.junior.browser.browser``) owns the connection and the page automation primitives; this module adds the tab primitives it deliberately does not cover, operating on a connected ``Browser``: tabs = await list_tabs(browser) # every tab + active flag tab = await open_tab(browser, url) # new tab, navigated and focused tab = await switch_tab(browser, index) # move the AI (and the user) to it tab = await close_tab(browser, index) # close one, activate the next Keep-alive tab -------------- Chromium exits when its **last window closes**, and the container keeps running (the desktop session is still alive), so the live view stays up while the browser window is gone: neither the user nor the AI can reach the page again until the browser process is restarted. To make that impossible by accident, every session owns one **keep-alive tab** (``about:blank#codx-keep-alive``, titled "codx-junior · keep this tab open"): - ``ensure_keep_alive_tab`` creates it once and reactivates the working tab, so closing every other tab leaves the window (and Chromium) alive; - ``close_tab`` refuses to close it; - ``ensure_page`` reopens a page when, despite the guard, the browser ends up with no tabs at all (see ``BrowserManager.connect_browser`` for the full recovery of a dead browser). Conventions ----------- - the *tab index* is the position of the page in ``context.pages`` (stable while no tab is opened or closed); that is what the agent tools expose; - ``browser.page`` always points at the tab the AI drives; - every selection is brought to front, so the live view shows the tab the AI is working on (co-browsing); - the keep-alive tab and the last tab are never closed: closing them would close the browser window the user is watching. """ import logging from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) #: Hard cap on the tabs an agent may open (they are all visible to the user). MAX_TABS = 20 #: Fragment identifying the protected tab (survives reconnections). KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT = "codx-keep-alive" #: URL of the protected tab (``about:blank`` + marker fragment). KEEP_ALIVE_URL = f"about:blank#{KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT}" #: Title of the protected tab (what the user reads in the tab strip). KEEP_ALIVE_TITLE = "codx-junior · keep this tab open" #: Content of the protected tab: explains why it must stay open. KEEP_ALIVE_HTML = f""" {KEEP_ALIVE_TITLE}

{KEEP_ALIVE_TITLE}

This tab keeps the browser window open while you and the AI work. Do not close it: the browser (and this live view) would disappear.

codx-junior

""" #: Timeout (ms) used when restoring a page after the browser lost every tab. RECOVER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 def _session_label(browser) -> str: """Short session id used in the log lines (never raises).""" session = getattr(browser, "session", None) return str(getattr(session, "id", "") or "?")[:8] def _is_closed(page) -> bool: """Return True when the page is already closed (never raises).""" try: return bool(page.is_closed()) except Exception: return False def open_pages(browser) -> List[Any]: """ Return the open tabs of a connected browser. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. Returns: List[Any]: Playwright pages, in the browser's tab order. Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected. Example: >>> open_pages(browser) # doctest: +SKIP [] """ context = getattr(browser, "context", None) if context is None: raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected (call start_session first)") return [page for page in list(context.pages) if not _is_closed(page)] def page_url(page) -> str: """Return the page URL, or ``about:blank`` when it cannot be read.""" try: return page.url or "about:blank" except Exception: return "about:blank" def is_keep_alive_page(page) -> bool: """ Return True when *page* is the session's protected (keep-alive) tab. Args: page: Playwright page. Returns: bool: True when the page carries :data:`KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT`. Example: >>> is_keep_alive_page(page) # doctest: +SKIP True """ return KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT in page_url(page) def keep_alive_page(browser) -> Optional[Any]: """ Return the session's protected tab, or None when it does not exist. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. Returns: Optional[Any]: The keep-alive page, or None. """ for page in open_pages(browser): if is_keep_alive_page(page): return page return None def active_tab_index(browser, pages: Optional[List[Any]] = None) -> int: """ Return the index of the tab the AI is driving. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. pages: Already resolved tab list (avoids a second lookup). Returns: int: Index in ``pages``, or -1 when there are no tabs. """ pages = open_pages(browser) if pages is None else pages page = getattr(browser, "page", None) for index, candidate in enumerate(pages): if candidate is page: return index return len(pages) - 1 if pages else -1 def page_index(browser, page) -> int: """Return the position of *page* in the tab list (-1 when not tracked).""" try: return open_pages(browser).index(page) except (ValueError, RuntimeError): return -1 async def describe_tab(browser, page, index: int) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Build the tab descriptor returned to the agent tools. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser` (used to flag the active tab). page: Playwright page. index: Position of the page in the tab list. Returns: Dict with ``index``, ``id``, ``url``, ``title``, ``active``, ``closed`` and ``keep_alive``. """ url = page_url(page) try: title = (await page.title()) or "" except Exception: title = "" return { "index": index, "id": f"tab-{index}", "url": url, "title": title.strip(), "active": page is getattr(browser, "page", None), "closed": _is_closed(page), "keep_alive": is_keep_alive_page(page), } async def _sync_location(browser, page) -> None: """ Mirror the tab URL/title into the session (summaries, audit and UI read it). Kept out of ``Browser`` on purpose: tab handling must not depend on that class' private helpers. """ session = getattr(browser, "session", None) if session is None: return try: session.current_url = page.url or session.current_url except Exception: pass try: session.current_title = await page.title() except Exception: pass try: session.mark_active() except Exception: pass async def _activate(browser, page) -> None: """Make *page* the page the AI drives and the tab the user sees.""" browser.page = page try: await page.bring_to_front() except Exception as ex: # Not fatal: the tab is still drivable, only the focus hint was lost. logger.debug("bring_to_front failed: %s", ex) await _sync_location(browser, page) async def ensure_page(browser, restore: bool = True): """ Return a drivable page, recreating one when every tab was closed. Chromium can be left with zero tabs (the user closed them all). The browser process may still be alive, so instead of failing every subsequent action a fresh tab is opened (restoring the session's last URL when asked). Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. restore: Navigate the new tab to ``session.current_url`` (default). Returns: Page: The page the AI must drive (``browser.page`` is updated). Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected. """ context = getattr(browser, "context", None) if context is None: raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected (call start_session first)") pages = open_pages(browser) if pages: current = getattr(browser, "page", None) if current in pages: return current browser.page = pages[-1] return browser.page page = await context.new_page() browser.page = page session = getattr(browser, "session", None) target = (getattr(session, "current_url", None) or "").strip() if restore else "" if target and target not in ("about:blank", "chrome://newtab/"): try: await page.goto(target, wait_until="load", timeout=RECOVER_TIMEOUT_MS) except Exception as ex: logger.warning("Could not restore '%s' after reopening a tab: %s", target, ex) await _sync_location(browser, page) logger.warning( "Session %s had no tabs left; reopened %s", _session_label(browser), target or "about:blank", ) return page async def ensure_keep_alive_tab(browser) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: """ Make sure the protected tab that keeps the browser window open exists. The tab is created once per session and never activated: the tab the AI is driving (and the user is watching) keeps the focus. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. Returns: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: Descriptor of the protected tab, or None when it cannot be created (the session keeps working without it). Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected. """ context = getattr(browser, "context", None) if context is None: raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected (call start_session first)") existing = keep_alive_page(browser) if existing is not None: return await describe_tab(browser, existing, page_index(browser, existing)) previous = getattr(browser, "page", None) if previous is not None and _is_closed(previous): previous = None try: page = await context.new_page() try: await page.goto(KEEP_ALIVE_URL, wait_until="load", timeout=RECOVER_TIMEOUT_MS) except Exception as ex: logger.debug("Could not open %s: %s", KEEP_ALIVE_URL, ex) try: # Gives the tab its title/explanation (the URL keeps the marker) await page.set_content(KEEP_ALIVE_HTML) except Exception as ex: logger.debug("Could not set the keep-alive content: %s", ex) except Exception as ex: logger.warning("Could not create the keep-alive tab: %s", ex) return None if previous is not None: # Keep driving (and showing) the tab that was active before await _activate(browser, previous) else: browser.page = page logger.info("Keep-alive tab ready for session %s", _session_label(browser)) return await describe_tab(browser, page, page_index(browser, page)) async def list_tabs(browser) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """ Return every open tab; the one the AI drives carries ``active: True``. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. Returns: List[Dict[str, Any]]: One descriptor per tab, in tab order. Example: >>> await list_tabs(browser) # doctest: +SKIP [{'index': 0, 'url': 'https://example.com', 'active': True, ...}] """ if not open_pages(browser): await ensure_page(browser) pages = open_pages(browser) return [await describe_tab(browser, page, index) for index, page in enumerate(pages)] async def open_tab(browser, url: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Open a new tab, focus it and (optionally) navigate to *url*. The current tab is left untouched, so the agent can keep a reference page open while working on another one. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. url: Optional URL opened in the new tab (``file:///home//...`` works for shared project folders). Returns: Dict[str, Any]: Descriptor of the new (now active) tab. Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected or :data:`MAX_TABS` is already reached. RuntimeError: When the navigation fails. """ pages = open_pages(browser) if len(pages) >= MAX_TABS: raise RuntimeError( f"Too many open tabs ({len(pages)}); close one with close_tab first" ) context = getattr(browser, "context", None) page = await context.new_page() await _activate(browser, page) if url: # navigate() keeps the networkidle -> load fallback and syncs the session await browser.navigate(url) index = active_tab_index(browser) logger.info( "Opened tab %s (%s) in session %s", index, url or "about:blank", _session_label(browser), ) return await describe_tab(browser, page, index) async def switch_tab(browser, index: Optional[int] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Make the tab at *index* the one the AI drives and the user sees. Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. index: Tab index (0-based). ``None`` keeps the active tab. Returns: Dict[str, Any]: Descriptor of the selected tab. Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected. ValueError: When *index* is not a number or is out of range. """ if not open_pages(browser): await ensure_page(browser) pages = open_pages(browser) if index is None: target = active_tab_index(browser, pages) else: try: target = int(index) except (TypeError, ValueError): raise ValueError(f"tab index '{index}' is not a number") if target < 0 or target >= len(pages): raise ValueError(f"tab index {index} is out of range (0-{len(pages) - 1})") page = pages[target] await _activate(browser, page) logger.info("Switched to tab %s of session %s", target, _session_label(browser)) return await describe_tab(browser, page, target) async def close_tab(browser, index: Optional[int] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Close a tab and activate the one that takes its place. Two tabs are protected: the last one (closing it closes the window the user is watching) and the keep-alive tab (closing it removes the protection that keeps Chromium alive when the user closes everything else). Args: browser: Connected :class:`Browser`. index: Tab index (0-based). ``None`` closes the active tab. Returns: Dict[str, Any]: Descriptor of the newly active tab plus ``closed_index``, ``closed_url`` and ``closed_title``. Raises: RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected, has no tabs, only one tab is left, or the selected tab is the keep-alive tab. ValueError: When *index* is not a number or is out of range. """ pages = open_pages(browser) if not pages: raise RuntimeError("The browser has no open tabs") if len(pages) <= 1: raise RuntimeError( "Cannot close the last tab: it would close the browser window the user " "is watching. Navigate it somewhere else or open another tab first" ) if index is None: target = active_tab_index(browser, pages) else: try: target = int(index) except (TypeError, ValueError): raise ValueError(f"tab index '{index}' is not a number") if target < 0 or target >= len(pages): raise ValueError(f"tab index {index} is out of range (0-{len(pages) - 1})") page = pages[target] if is_keep_alive_page(page): raise RuntimeError( "Refusing to close the keep-alive tab: it prevents the browser window " "from disappearing. Work in another tab instead of closing this one" ) closed = await describe_tab(browser, page, target) await page.close() remaining = open_pages(browser) if not remaining: # Should not happen (the keep-alive tab is protected and the tab count was # checked), but never leave the session without a page. await ensure_page(browser) remaining = open_pages(browser) # The tab that now occupies the freed position becomes active next_index = min(target, len(remaining) - 1) await _activate(browser, remaining[next_index]) logger.info( "Closed tab %s of session %s (active tab: %s)", target, _session_label(browser), next_index, ) result = await describe_tab(browser, remaining[next_index], next_index) result["closed_index"] = target result["closed_url"] = closed.get("url") result["closed_title"] = closed.get("title") return result def format_tabs(tabs: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str: """ Render tabs as one line each, marking the active tab with ``*``. Args: tabs: Descriptors returned by :func:`list_tabs`. Returns: str: Plain text listing (``*`` = tab the AI is driving). Example: >>> print(format_tabs([{"index": 0, "title": "A", "url": "https://a", "active": True}])) * [0] A — https://a """ if not tabs: return "(no open tabs)" lines = [] for tab in tabs: marker = "*" if tab.get("active") else "-" title = tab.get("title") or "(untitled)" suffix = " [keep-alive: do not close]" if tab.get("keep_alive") else "" lines.append( f"{marker} [{tab.get('index')}] {title} — {tab.get('url') or 'about:blank'}{suffix}" ) return "\n".join(lines) # Made with ❤️ by codx-junior """ BrowserManager — CRUD operations for browser sessions. Manages session lifecycle: create, read, update, delete. Handles persistence in Chat.meta_data and Docker container management. Follows the workspace pattern: .codx/browser_sessions//.session A session is created with a human-readable ``name`` and may be shared by several chats (``session.chat_ids``). The container is a Chromium instance with a live VNC view (for the user) and a CDP endpoint (for the AI), so both actors control the same browser page. Folder sharing -------------- Any number of project folders are mounted inside the browser container under a single tree (``/home//``) and the browser downloads are written inside the default folder, so the user and the AI exchange files with the project instead of being locked in the container: - ``configure_share`` decides the mounts when the session is created; - the downloads folder is applied through CDP on every connection (``Browser.setDownloadBehavior``), because it is browser-wide state; - ``get_shared_paths`` / ``get_shared_files`` expose the mapping and the files the browser saved inside the project. Browser window survival ----------------------- Chromium exits when its last window (tab) is closed, while the container keeps running: the live view stays up but the browser window is gone and the DevTools endpoint is dead. Two defences keep a session usable: - a protected **keep-alive tab** is created with the session and ensured on every connection (``codx/junior/browser/tabs.py``), so closing every other tab leaves the window alive; - ``connect_browser`` **recovers** a dead browser by restarting the container entrypoint (which relaunches Chromium with the mounted profile) and retrying the connection once. Lifecycle primitives -------------------- - ``create_session(name, chat_id, initial_url, description)`` : start a new container + persist metadata. - ``stop_session(session_id)`` : stop the container but KEEP it (restartable). - ``restart_session(session_id)`` : relaunch Chromium (recovery) / recreate a stopped session. - ``delete_session(session_id)`` : stop the container, remove it and the folder. - ``log_activity(...)`` : append an audit entry for a user/AI action. """ import logging import os import json import asyncio from datetime import datetime from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, List, Set from pathlib import Path from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings from codx.junior.browser.model import BrowserSession from codx.junior.browser.docker_browser_manager import DockerBrowserManager from codx.junior.browser.browser import Browser, run_coroutine_sync from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs from codx.junior.browser.activity import BrowserActivityLog logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) BROWSER_SESSIONS_DIR = "browser_sessions" SESSION_FILE_EXTENSION = ".session" #: Hard cap applied to the shared-files listing. MAX_SHARED_FILES = 500 #: References to the background tasks started outside a request (keep-alive tab). _background_tasks: Set[Any] = set() def _is_inside(path: str, base: str) -> bool: """Return True when *path* is inside *base* (both may be relative).""" try: return os.path.commonpath( [os.path.abspath(path), os.path.abspath(base)] ) == os.path.abspath(base) except ValueError: return False def _spawn_background(coroutine) -> None: """ Schedule *coroutine* on the running loop, keeping a reference until it ends. """
DockerBrowserManager — manages the Chromium co-browsing container lifecycle.

Each ``BrowserSession`` gets its own LinuxServer.io Chromium container.  The
container serves two endpoints:

* **Live view / user control** – the Selkies web desktop on port ``3000``,
  published through Traefik at ``/browser/<session_id>/``.  Users can click,
  type and navigate exactly like a local browser.
* **DevTools automation** – Chromium's CDP endpoint.  Chromium binds it to
  ``127.0.0.1`` only, so a small TCP proxy (``browser/cdp_proxy.py``) listens
  on the container network at port ``9223`` and forwards to ``9222``.  The API
  container (same Docker network) uses it through Playwright.

Lifecycle semantics
-------------------
- ``stop_container(session, remove=True)``  : stop + remove (full teardown).
- ``stop_container(session, remove=False)`` : stop only — the container is kept
  so it can be started again with ``restart_container`` (state preserved).
- ``restart_container(session)``            : starts an existing (stopped)
  container, or recreates it if the container no longer exists.

Project folder sharing
----------------------
``configure_share`` maps any number of project folders into the container before
the ``docker run`` command is built, so the user (live view) and the AI exchange
files with the project:

- every selected folder is bind mounted under a single tree,
  ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` (the project root, when mounted, *is*
  ``/home/<project_name>``), optionally read-only per folder;
- the downloads folder is a project folder too: when it lives inside one of the
  mounted folders the browser writes there directly, otherwise it gets its own
  bind at ``/downloads``.  ``Browser.setDownloadBehavior`` points Chromium to it.

Configuration (environment variables)
-------------------------------------
``CODX_BROWSER_IMAGE``            Chromium image (default
                                  ``lscr.io/linuxserver/chromium:latest``).
``CODX_BROWSER_NETWORK``          Docker network (default
                                  ``codx-junior_default``).
``CODX_BROWSER_AUTO_PULL``        Pull the image when missing (default ``1``).
``CODX_BROWSER_SHARE_PROJECT``    Mount project folders (default ``1``).
``CODX_BROWSER_HOME_ROOT``        Container root of the project tree
                                  (default ``/home``).
``CODX_BROWSER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL``  Override the public VNC base URL.
``CODX_BROWSER_AUTH_MIDDLEWARE``  Traefik auth middleware name

When clicking "chat" if there's no exiting latest chat it must show the dialog to link a chat or create new one. Now it does nothing.

About keep chromium open I'm sure there settings to force chrome to don't close and always keep an open tab. 

----
Chromium has no native Enterprise Policy that prevents the browser window from closing when the user closes the last tab. By design, closing the final tab always closes the browser window. [1] (https://www.systutorials.com/prevent-chrome-closing-after-closing-the-last-tab/), [2] (https://www.rabbitpair.com/en/blog/chrome-lock-tab-prevent-accidental-close)
However, you can combine Enterprise Policies (to keep the background process alive and force specific tabs on launch) with a force-installed extension (to intercept the last-tab close event and immediately open a fresh tab). [1] (https://gpedit.tplant.com.au/en-us/policy/chrome/BackgroundModeEnabled/), [2] (https://www.systutorials.com/prevent-chrome-closing-after-closing-the-last-tab/)

1. Enterprise Policy JSON Example

On Linux, save this file to /etc/chromium/policies/managed/keep_open.json. (On Windows, apply these same keys under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Chromium). [1] (https://chromium.googlesource.com/playground/chromium-org-site/+/6cfcc327e21c6a782ee282a4787e308215bd0df8/administrators/policy-list-3/index.md), [2] (https://gpedit.tplant.com.au/en-us/policy/chrome/BackgroundModeEnabled/)
json
{
  "BackgroundModeEnabled": true,
  "RestoreOnStartup": 4,
  "RestoreOnStartupURLs": [
    "about:blank"
  ],
  "ExtensionInstallForcelist": [
    "dlnpfhfhmkiebpnlllpehlmklgdggbhn;https://google.com"
  ]
}
Use code with caution.

How Each Policy Works

• BackgroundModeEnabled (true): Keeps the Chromium background process and session alive in the system tray even if all windows are closed.
• RestoreOnStartup (4) & RestoreOnStartupURLs: Forces Chromium to always launch with a specific tab (such as about:blank or your automation dashboard) whenever a new window opens.
• ExtensionInstallForcelist: Silently installs and locks an extension that the user cannot disable. The ID dlnpfhfhmkiebpnlllpehlmklgdggbhn corresponds to Don't Close Window With Last Tab, which automatically spawns a pinned tab whenever the user tries to close the final tab so the window never exits. (Note: If your automated Chromium lacks Google Web Store access, point the URL to your own self-hosted .crx update manifest). [1] (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/dont-close-window-with-la/dlnpfhfhmkiebpnlllpehlmklgdggbhn), [2] (https://chromium.googlesource.com/playground/chromium-org-site/+/6cfcc327e21c6a782ee282a4787e308215bd0df8/administrators/policy-list-3/index.md), [3] (https://gpedit.tplant.com.au/en-us/policy/chrome/BackgroundModeEnabled/), [4] (https://issues.chromium.org/40223461)

2. Alternative: Kiosk Mode (No Tab Closing Possible)

If your automation only needs a single full-screen interface and you want to completely remove the user's ability to close tabs or windows, bypass policies and launch Chromium with the kiosk flag:
bash
chromium --kiosk "https://your-target-url.com"
Use code with caution.
Note: In kiosk mode, standard window controls and tab close buttons are hidden, requiring Alt+F4 or process termination to exit.

Verification

After placing the JSON file or setting the registry keys, open chrome://policy in your Chromium instance and click Reload policies to confirm the status shows OK. [1] (https://issues.chromium.org/40223461), [2] (https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41161685)
